Hi all,

I am Ping-Ju, an incoming PhD student in Economics at Toulouse. I have a background in Applied Math and have recently been exploring Lean 4 through the Natural Number Game.

I am interested in building a foundational library for Microeconomic Theory. My goal is to formalize common objects and assumptions used in research, such as: Preference & Utility, Information Structure, Contract Theory, Mechanism Design.

My ultimate goal is to create a "toolbox" that allows economists to use these properties as Typeclasses or Tactics without re-proving measure-theoretic details every time.

Is anyone here already working on formalizing economic theory, decision theory, or game theory in Lean 4?

I would love to connect, exchange thoughts, and avoid duplicating efforts if a project or working group already exists. If you are interested in this intersection of economics and Lean, or have advice on where a beginner should start with these topics, I would love to chat!

Looking forward to learning from you all.
Using Lean for economics seems like such an obviously smart idea.. I wonder how many other economic projects are being done here?

Hi Ian,
I feel the same way. I just searched a few keywords, but didn't see something related to economics. Let me know if you have more information

Hi Ping-Ju,

I'm also fairly new here and just finished the Natural Number Game recently! I have a similar interest — mainly macro theory, but micro excites me too.

I actually tried formalizing Arrow's Impossibility Theorem as a learning exercise. The preference relation part might be relevant to what you're thinking about: https://github.com/ChihChengLiang/arrow/blob/main/Arrow/Arrow.lean

I also came across this game theory repo that seems to have gone quiet: https://github.com/wpoverman/lean4-game-theory

Would love to follow along with what you're building, and happy to help where I can!

I saw your works! Very incredible. My area is close to IO/ micro theory. Recently I didn't have time enough to really coding by myself. So I hope in the summer I could have more progress. keep in touch
